images.title: Three glasses, four friends
images.purpose: Set up the question: 4 friends share 3 glasses of juice equally; how much does each friend drink?
images.composition: A row of three full glasses at the top and a row of four empty cups below, with wide space between the rows.
images.exact_structure: Top: 3 tall glasses of exactly the same size in a row, each full of juice filled amber #E69F00, each marked by 3 grey #6B7280 level lines into 4 exactly equal layers. Below: 4 empty cups of exactly the same size in a row, outlined teal #0072B2, one for each friend. The first cup outlined in reddish purple #CC79A7 with a question label. No fraction written anywhere. Exactly 3 glasses, 4 equal layers in each, 4 cups.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any juice drawn in the cups, any fraction written in the frame, or glass layers of unequal height
images.takeaway: Share every glass equally among the 4 friends.
images.description: Three full glasses of juice, each marked into 4 equal layers, above 4 empty cups for 4 friends, the first cup marked ? glass each.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one layer in each glass and say how many layers one friend gets in all.

image_decisions.why: Glasses marked in equal layers above the friends' empty cups show how to share each glass, without the answer.
